I was having a discussion with a coworker about the FPH ban, and the question came up of "What company DOESN'T have a vested interest in keeping people fat?".

Coworker and I ruled out any food company right away, along with anyone who makes diet products. Then we got into a good discussion of whether Protien World has an active interest (which, it seems like they'd have a partial interest, as it means repeat / revolving door customers).

Essentially, the only companies we could think of that have no vested interest in fats is anywhere that has a lot of seating or rides, like concert venues and airlines. (We couldn't include theme parks, as they'd rather butter-huffers waddle around all day then ride the rides, I'm sure).

Can anyone else think of other places?
Who DOESN'T have a vested interest in keeping people fat?

Mass producing clothing/fashion industry is a big one I can think of. Big people = more material = higher cost of production all around (from increased shipment weight/heavier truck loads, increased material usage, need for larger space to store inventory, longer production time especially if fabric is so big it gets caught in shit, etc). Of course you can charge more for your products to offset costs, but the higher you price the smaller your market or profit margin.

Companies that don't want to end up paying/subsidizing workers' health care costs of obesity-related diseases/issues. Services areas where fit people are practically required for the job, or require fit people to get into tight spaces. Companies where you need productive/alert staff, not lazy food-preoccupied staff.

Some restaurant businesses like buffets.
As for resturaunts in my experience skinny in shape people can usually eat more food then a fatty.

Could most likely be. I mean if I know I'm going to a buffet for dinner, I'll skip breakfast and eat something small for lunch just enough to satisfy me, so I can go all-out for a dinner buffet. So that does make sense in a way. Like how a lot of competitive eaters who win are normal sized rather than obese/fat.

I bet fat people tend to load themselves up with cheap crap like soda at buffets too.

Yeah but fatties will visit more often. I might head to a BurgerFi or Five Guys once in a blue moon. I'll skip breakfast/lunch to be able to have a triple stack and some onion rings but I won't go again for a long while. Some butter huffers will visit a place multiple times a week.
That's a lot more reassuring than what we could think of, thanks!

I can offer a bit of an ambivalent answer...

I run my own Biohazard Remediation business (i.e. Crime Scene Cleanup).

While I’m an advocate for personal life choice yet despise gluttony, it’s a major generation of profit for the industry as a whole, and will continue to be in the future. The trend in the past few years has been cleaning up after baby boomers who are overweight, in ill health, and are recluses — it results in a lot of unattended death scenarios (rotting corpses).

Do I hate having to deal with consoling family members and hunting down next of kin and sympathizing with their loss? Absolutely. But at the same time I just have a “fuck it” attitude for these cases and feel they’re ultimately deserving of their fate.

I can’t say the industry has a vested interest in keeping people fat, but indirectly the fat SOB’s will keep my pockets full and provide PLENTY of jobs in the future!

Actually, any company who thinks about the future wouldn't want to keep people fat. It's much better to have customers who keep spending a small amount on your products for a long time than to have them spend a lot for a brief time. The shortened lifespans of the obese, not to mention the extra money they spend on other things (healthcare, food, clothes), makes them much worse customers in the long run for many companies.

In all honesty, your employer and healthcare companies have a huge interest in keeping you slim. The reality is that fatties cost more and if costs go up so do your employer's costs. Especially now with HObama care forcing every full time employee to be given healthcare.
I guess crematories are another one considering all the stories of how much of a hassle it is to dispose of fat people.
Having to burn the body longer probably costs them a ton in gas bills.
I still remember the story about the crematorium going up in flames because a 500lbs corpse burned up too quickly.

Do you think they could burn the fat bodies to heat the place in winter? I bet they get enough dead fats from heart attacks and what not that they could keep warm almost all winter. Once you reach ignition temperature the fat should burn by itself and produce energy.

I would argue that any government has a vested interest in keeping people healthy because a healthy person should contribute way more in taxes and productivity over their lifetime than an obeast would. With a disgusting blob you're missing out on a lot of productive working years from 30 to 60 to make up for the money invested in education and whatnot from 6 to 18~22. That's almost certainly a net loss.

Yeah, but they're not paying out pensions to those people. So they put in 10-20 years of work, then die before they can withdrawl anything from social security. Unless they soak up disability the entire time. Or, there's a government run healthcare system.

I guess it depends on the government.
It seems to me most places these days are not offering much in the way of pensions. I hadn't even considered it, but I'd still wager the disability hit would be worse.

Insurance companies would probably be better off due to the fact that keeping people living long and healthier increases their ability to pay longer on their premiums. Someone out there who knows how insurance algorithms for life expectancy work could probably give a viable explanation.

Car companies might be another one. I assume fatties automatically avoid certain cars because they can't ride comfortably in them, fit four feet of seatbelt extenders, etc. Also motorcycle companies?

Gyms? I know they need fatties to sign up every January 1st and the occasional life changing fatty. If you want people to maintain their gym membership for longer than 3 months don't you want them to be fit, thus causing them to continue using your gym to stay fit?
